Subject: Questions on pen-test phasing + SOC2 evidence cadence

Hi Marissa —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Legal & Security on our side reviewed the redline you shared and have three concrete asks before we can route for procurement:

1) Pen-test phasing: we need clarity on whether Redwood requires access to prod for the initial pentest or if a staged (staging/pre-prod) approach is acceptable. If prod access is required, we need a narrow timebox and escort/forensics constraints.
2) SOC 2 / evidence: can you confirm the cadence for sharing SOC2 artifacts and the expected turnaround for ad-hoc evidence requests?
3) Mutual action plan (MAP): procurement asked for a simple MAP with milestones (order form signature, SOC2 delivery, pen-test window, evidence delivery).

Can you send a proposed MAP + brief ops note on how you typically sequence pen tests for customers in our vertical? We can share preferred windows but need your recommended defaults.

Attachments we expect from your side: SOC2 summary, sample pen-test scope, and a draft MAP.

Appreciate it — ideally this week so we can keep the procurement cadence moving.

— Samir

Subject: Re: Questions on pen-test phasing + SOC2 evidence cadence

Samir — thanks for laying this out clearly. I put together a lightweight MAP and operational notes attached (MAP-pen-test-phasing.xlsx, RDW-Security-Exhibit-Draft_v3.pdf, SOC2-summary.pdf). Topline answers below and a suggested sequence we use for customers in regulated healthcare:

- Pen-test phasing (recommended default): Redwood prefers an initial staging/pre-prod pentest window for first-time customers. We can run a scoped production assessment only if the customer requires it; when production is used we require a 48-hour earliest notice and a 48-hour blackout window for maintenance, with limited blast radius and read-only access whenever possible.

- Forensics & access: production pentests require a named point-of-contact, ephemeral credentials where possible, and a forensics-first escalation path. We include standard RACI items in the MAP.

- SOC2 / evidence cadence: we provide a SOC2 summary (attached) immediately on request and can provide a redacted full report under an NDA. For ad-hoc evidence requests (log exports, config screenshots) our SLT target is to return within 10 business days for standard asks; for high-priority operational evidence (incident triage) we aim for 48–72 hours.

- Evidence delivery mechanism: weekly evidence bundles via a shared Drive folder during the active onboarding window; after onboarding we support on-demand evidence pulls (ticket + 10 business day SLA) or a retained evidence package per quarter.

- Order-form / exhibit redline notes: the attached security exhibit draft reflects our preference for a bounded inspection window, explicit staging carveouts, and a single annual vendor-initiated pen-test (customer may request additional tests under a separate SOW). See comment in the PDF on Section 3.2 (audit scope).

Next steps I propose:
1) Review attached MAP and redline with your procurement/legal and flag any non-starters.
2) Karthik (cc'd once legal weighs in) will propose specific contract language where necessary.
3) If acceptable, we schedule a 30-minute ops sync to lock windows (I can host 4/20 or 4/21).

I left an inline note in the MAP recommending a two-week staging window followed by an optional prod window (if needed) two weeks later. If you have preferred dates, drop them into the MAP and I will confirm capacity with our ops team.

Cheers,

Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Hi Samir / Marissa — quick legal review and suggested contract language below. I kept it tight so procurement can move fast; frank feedback welcome.

Redline summary (high level):
- Audit scope: we will accept a bounded audit limited to the Security Exhibit and the specific services called out in the Order Form. We will not agree to open-ended inspection of unrelated systems.
- Pen-test access: proposed clause — "Customer shall conduct penetration testing against Customer-designated test environments. Redwood will allow access to non-production environments. Production penetration tests require 14-days advance notice, defined blast-radius, and are limited to a single authenticated test per 12-month period unless otherwise agreed in writing."
- Forensics / data access: to protect multi-tenant telemetry we propose that Redwood provide sanitized logs and scoped forensic exports; Redwood will not provide raw underlying storage snapshots or unrestricted access to multi-tenant control planes.
- Evidence cadence: propose adding the following operative language to the Security Exhibit: "Standard evidence requests will be fulfilled within 10 business days. Emergency operational evidence related to incident response will be prioritized and fulfilled within 72 hours where feasible."

I inserted inline redlines in RDW-Security-Exhibit-Draft_v3.pdf and created a short supporting memo (see link in related_links). Specific asks for Acme Health to consider:
1) Limit production pentest to a short, mutually agreed window with an agreed rollback plan.
2) Agree on the format of evidence (redacted pdf bundles + Drive folder) to avoid repeated ad-hoc exports.
3) If Acme requires raw system-level access or unredacted logs, that should be scoped to a separate SOW and subject to additional indemnities.

If these high-level points work for you, I can produce a tracked MSA/Order Form redline for your counsel to iterate on.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Staff Counsel | Redwood Inference
